publications.authors: J Qing, HB Moss, T Dhaene, I Couckuyt
publications.venue: 17th Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS), 2023

publications.title: Finding knees in bayesian multi-objective optimization
publications.authors: A Heidari, J Qing, S Rojas Gonzalez, J Branke, T Dhaene, I Couckuyt
publications.venue: International Conference on Parallel Problem Solving from Nature, 104-117, 2022
publications.tldr: This paper proposes novel acquisition functions within a Bayesian Optimization framework to efficiently find knee points in multi-objective optimization. Acknowledging that decision-makers often prefer specific trade-offs over the full Pareto front, the approach detects knees (based on two definitions) with limited evaluations. This method scales to many objectives, demonstrating promising results on various benchmarks for identifying desirable solutions data-efficiently.
publications.abstract: Multi-objective optimization requires many evaluations to identify a sufficiently dense approximation of the Pareto front. Especially for a higher number of objectives, extracting the Pareto front might not be easy nor cheap. On the other hand, the Decision-Maker is not always interested in the entire Pareto front, and might prefer a solution where there is a desirable trade-off between different objectives. An example of an attractive solution is the knee point of the Pareto front, although the current literature differs on the definition of a knee. In this work, we propose to detect knee solutions in a data-efficient manner (i.e., with a limited number of time-consuming evaluations), according to two definitions of knees. In particular, we propose several novel acquisition functions in the Bayesian Optimization framework for detecting these knees, which allows for scaling to many objectives. The suggested acquisition functions are evaluated on various benchmarks with promising results.

publications.title: Adaptive sampling with automatic stopping for feasible region identification in engineering design
publications.authors: J Qing, N Knudde, F Garbuglia, D Spina, I Couckuyt, T Dhaene
publications.tldr: This paper introduces an adaptive sampling methodology using Gaussian process metamodels for efficient feasible region identification in engineering design problems with multiple constraints. It employs an information-based sequential sampling strategy for refining prediction accuracy. A novel contribution is a framework for automatically stopping the adaptive sampling process by accurately estimating the metamodel's prediction accuracy, demonstrating improved efficiency and robustness compared to state-of-the-art methods.
publications.abstract: Engineering design is a complex process to find a suitable trade-off among different, and sometimes conflicting, design specifications. In reality, these requirements can be often considered as constraints of the design problem, that can be defined in terms of performance measures or geometrical characteristics of the device under study. In this paper, a new design space exploration methodology is presented for discovering feasible regions in the design space, where the term feasible region indicates the set of all design configurations satisfying all constraints of the design problem. The proposed method is based on Gaussian process metamodels to estimate the feasible region and leverages a information-based adaptive sampling technique to sequentially refine the prediction accuracy, which is applicable for multiple constraints problems. To efficiently stop the adaptive sampling process, a novel framework to estimate the metamodel’s prediction accuracy is proposed. The efficiency, accuracy and robustness of the proposed approach are compared with state-of-art techniques on suitable benchmark problems and practical engineering examples.

publications.title: A robust Bayesian optimization framework for microwave circuit design under uncertainty
publications.authors: D De Witte, J Qing, I Couckuyt, T Dhaene, D Vande Ginste, D Spina
publications.tldr: This paper presents a robust Bayesian Optimization (BO) framework for microwave circuit design addressing parameter uncertainty. It achieves robustness by modifying the expected improvement (EI) criterion to account for design variations. The data-efficient BO minimizes simulations while identifying robust designs. Validation demonstrates significantly improved design robustness compared to standard methods.
publications.abstract: In modern electronics, there are many inevitable uncertainties and variations of design parameters that have a profound effect on the performance of a device. These are, among others, induced by manufacturing tolerances, assembling inaccuracies, material diversities, machining errors, etc. This prompts wide interests in enhanced optimization algorithms that take the effect of these uncertainty sources into account and that are able to find robust designs, i.e., designs that are insensitive to the uncertainties early in the design cycle. In this work, a novel machine learning-based optimization framework that accounts for uncertainty of the design parameters is presented. This is achieved by using a modified version of the expected improvement criterion. Moreover, a data-efficient Bayesian Optimization framework is leveraged to limit the number of simulations required to find a robust design solution. Two suitable application examples validate that the robustness is significantly improved compared to standard design methods.

publications.title: Spectral representation of robustness measures for optimization under input uncertainty
publications.authors: J Qing, T Dhaene, I Couckuyt
publications.tldr: This paper proposes a Spectral Representation of Robustness Measures for efficient inference of mean-variance robustness under Gaussian Processes (GPs), circumventing challenging Bayesian variance inference. Leveraging GP spectral representation with Fourier features, this analytical approach approximates robustness for normal and uniform input uncertainties. Integrated into robust Bayesian Optimization acquisition functions, the method demonstrates competitive performance on benchmarks and real-world applications, effectively quantifying and optimizing for robustness.
publications.abstract: We study the inference of mean-variance robustness measures to quantify input uncertainty under the Gaussian Process (GP) framework. These measures are widely used in applications where the robustness of the solution is of interest, for example, in engineering design. While the variance is commonly used to characterize the robustness, Bayesian inference of the variance using GPs is known to be challenging. In this paper, we propose a Spectral Representation of Robustness Measures based on the GP’s spectral representation, i.e., an analytical approach to approximately infer both robustness measures for normal and uniform input uncertainty distributions. We present two approximations based on different Fourier features and compare their accuracy numerically. To demonstrate their utility and efficacy in robust Bayesian Optimization, we integrate the analytical robustness measures in three standard acquisition functions for various robust optimization formulations. We show their competitive performance on numerical benchmarks and real-life applications.

publications.title: Hovering efficiency optimization of the ducted propeller with weight penalty taken into account
publications.authors: Y Hu, J xiang Qing, ZH Liu, ZJ Conrad, JN Cao, XP Zhang
publications.tldr: This paper optimizes ducted propeller design for hovering efficiency, incorporating structural weight. It finds that weight penalty is crucial at low disk loading, favoring lighter structures, while aerodynamic efficiency dominates at high disk loading. Multi-objective optimization identifies designs where ducted propellers still surpass open propellers in system efficiency at low disk loadings. Optimal configurations feature a large inner lip (most impactful for efficiency), small outer lip, and short/no diffuser, achieving significant weight reduction with limited aerodynamic loss, leading to low height-to-diameter ratios for easier integration.
publications.abstract: The ducted propeller is superior to the open propeller in hovering efficiency. However, the overall system efficiency of a ducted propeller is reduced due to its heavy structure. If the weight penalty is taken into account, will the ducted propeller still be superior to an open propeller? And in this scenario, how will a ducted propeller with better efficiency than an open propeller be designed? This paper investigates these questions by parametric analysis based on experiments and then parametric optimization that involves hovering efficiency and structural weight in objective functions. Both multi-disciplinary design optimization and multi-objective programming are performed by surrogate-based optimization. An in-house automatic structured mesh generation module is developed to deal with significant geometry variation in design space. Finally, the optimization results are validated by post-optimization experiments. The results of experiment and optimization indicate that the effects of weight penalty play a leading role at low disk loading and hence in this case, the one with lighter structure is superior. But at high disk loading, as thrust gets higher, the leading factor turns into aerodynamic hovering efficiency, therefore the one with higher aerodynamic hovering efficiency prevails. The multi-objective optimization produces an L-shaped Pareto front, and the optimum of multi-disciplinary optimization is quite close to the Pareto front knee point. The designs in this region encounter limited aerodynamic hovering efficiency loss but gain significant weight reduction. Therefore, we can obtain a ducted propeller superior to an open propeller in system efficiency with pretty low disk loading, although the weight penalty is considered. These designs feature a relatively large inner lip radius, a small outer lip radius, and a short or even no diffuser. This means that the inner lip radius contributes the most to the aerodynamic hovering efficiency, followed by the diffuser and outer lip. These designs have very low height to diameter ratio therefore they can be easily integrated into aircraft structure.

publications.title: Bayesian active learning for multi‐objective feasible region identification in microwave devices
publications.authors: F Garbuglia, J Qing, N Knudde, D Spina, I Couckuyt, D Deschrijver, ...
publications.tldr: This paper introduces a novel Bayesian active learning framework for efficient multi-objective feasible region identification in microwave device design. It leverages a stochastic model to accurately map designs satisfying specifications while significantly reducing the number of simulations required. The framework provides an automated and efficient procedure, validated through an application example demonstrating its effectiveness in rapidly discovering suitable device designs.
publications.abstract: In microwave device and circuit design, many simulations are often needed to find a set of designs that satisfy one or multiple specifications chosen by the designer upfront: the feasible region. A novel Bayesian active learning framework is presented to accurately identify the feasible region with a low number of simulations. The technique leverages on a stochastic model to obtain an efficient and automated procedure. A suitable application example validates the proposed technique and shows its effectiveness to rapidly obtain many suitable designs.

publications.title: Batch Bayesian active learning for feasible region identification by local penalization
publications.authors: J Qing, N Knudde, I Couckuyt, T Dhaene, K Shintani
publications.tldr: This paper introduces a batch Bayesian active learning technique for efficient feasible region identification, addressing the limitation of sequential sampling in expensive constraint evaluations. Leveraging available computational resources, the method selects multiple samples per iteration, assuming Lipschitz continuity of the constraint function. It also extends current state-of-the-art batch methods for this task. Experiments demonstrate the proposed technique's superior performance over these extended batch strategies.
publications.abstract: Identifying all designs satisfying a set of constraints is an important part of the engineering design process. With physics-based simulation codes, evaluating the constraints becomes considerable expensive. Active learning can provide an elegant approach to efficiently characterize the feasible region, i.e., the set of feasible designs. Although active learning strategies have been proposed for this task, most of them are dealing with adding just one sample per iteration as opposed to selecting multiple samples per iteration, also known as batch active learning. While this is efficient with respect to the amount of information gained per iteration, it neglects available computation resources. We propose a batch Bayesian active learning technique for feasible region identification by assuming that the constraint function is Lipschitz continuous. In addition, we extend current state-of-the-art batch methods to also handle feasible region identification. Experiments show better performance of the proposed method than the extended batch methods.

publications.title: Bayesian active learning for electromagnetic structure design
publications.authors: J Qing, N Knudde, I Couckuyt, D Spina, T Dhaene
publications.venue: 2020 14th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP), 1-5, 2020
publications.tldr: This paper presents a Bayesian active learning framework for designing electromagnetic structures. It leverages an entropy search-based strategy with a Gaussian Process model to efficiently identify design configurations that satisfy specific requirements. The core contribution is minimizing the number of time-consuming computer simulations or expensive experimental trials needed to achieve desired design specifications, thereby accelerating the design process.
publications.abstract: A novel design framework based on Bayesian active learning is presented in this contribution. The proposed approach allows one to identify a set of design configurations satisfying the chosen specification. In particular, the entropy search-based active learning strategy, which relies on a Gaussian Process model, is able to minimize the number of time-consuming computer simulations or expensive design trials necessary to reach this goal. A suitable application example validates the proposed method.

publications.title: Kriging Assisted Integrated Rotor-Duct Optimization for Ducted Fan in Hover
publications.authors: J Qing, Y Hu, Y Wang, Z Liu, X Fu, W Liu
publications.tldr: This paper presents a Kriging-assisted integrated rotor-duct optimization for ducted fans in hover, simultaneously optimizing both components using RANS. This approach addresses crucial rotor-duct interactions, unlike prior separate optimizations. Key findings reveal that integrated design improves hovering efficiency by obtaining blades with longer tip chords. This injects more momentum into the duct's boundary layer, suppressing flow separation and allowing for larger diffuser expansion angles, ultimately leading to superior overall performance.
publications.abstract: The design of ducted fan was primarily based on parametric analysis and the existing optimization design studies mainly focus on either the rotor or the duct alone. However, the interactions between the rotor and duct remarkably affects the performance of the ducted fan. Therefore, it has been expected that an integrated optimization such the rotor-duct interactions are involved could result in a better design. In this paper, the integrated rotor-duct optimization was performed. Then it was compared with several different optimized configurations. The Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes solver incorporated with momentum source method was adopted to predict performance of ducted fan and it was validated by force measurement experiments. The duct shape was parameterized by the FFD method and the blade shape was modeled by Bezier splines. A surrogate based optimization framework using Kriging model was developed. The hovering efficiency was set as the objective function subjecting to the thrust constraint. The optima from different optimized configurations were analyzed with the help of crossover studies. The analysis revealed that the improvement of the ducted fan hovering efficiency is primarily restricted by the flow separations in the duct. When the shape of both the rotor and duct was involved into the design optimization, the blade with longer chord at blade tip was obtained. This helps injecting more momentum into the boundary layer of the duct and the flow separation can be suppressed. Therefore, the integrated rotor-duct optimization produces the duct with larger diffuser expansion angle and better hovering efficiency.

2026.title: Small Data at Small Scales: Learning Nanoparticle Affinities from Sparse Physicochemical Datasets
2026.authors: GD Patrón, BP Stordy, J Qing, Z Sepahi, C Tsay

2026.title: Active Learning for Gaussian Process Regression Under Self-Induced Boltzmann Weights
2026.authors: J Qing, H Moss, M Sachs
2026.tldr: This paper addresses active learning for Gaussian Process Regression under self-induced Boltzmann distributions, where the target depends on the unknown function. They propose **AB-SID-iVAR**, a GP-based acquisition function that approximates this intractable Bayesian target in closed form, crucially avoiding partition function estimation. Applicable to both discrete and continuous domains, AB-SID-iVAR establishes sublinear convergence guarantees for terminal prediction error. Empirical results demonstrate superior performance in synthetic benchmarks, potential energy surface modeling, and drug discovery tasks.
2026.abstract: We consider the active learning problem where the goal is to learn an unknown function with low prediction error under an unknown Boltzmann distribution induced by the function itself. This self-induced weighting arises naturally in problems such as potential energy surface (PES) modeling in computational chemistry, yet poses unique challenges as the target distribution is unknown and its partition function is intractable. We propose \texttt{AB-SID-iVAR}, a Gaussian Process-based acquisition function that approximates the intractable Bayesian target distribution in closed form while avoiding partition function estimation, and is applicable to both discrete and continuous input domains. We also analyze a Thompson sampling alternative (\texttt{TS-SID-iVAR}) as a higher variance Monte Carlo variant. Despite the unknown target, under mild conditions, we establish that the terminal prediction error vanishes with high probability, and provide a tighter average-case guarantee. We demonstrate consistent improvements over existing approaches in this setting on synthetic benchmarks and real-world PES modeling and drug discovery tasks.

2026.title: Meta-learning for sample-efficient Bayesian optimisation of fed-batch processes
2026.authors: B Langdon, GD Patrón, CD Kappatou, RM Lee, B Shafei, J Qing, ...
2026.tldr: This paper proposes System-Aware Neural ODE Processes (SANODEP) as a meta-learning surrogate model for sample-efficient Bayesian Optimization (BayesOpt) of fed-batch processes. Addressing limitations of traditional GP-based BayesOpt in handling time-varying, stochastic batch fluctuations and cross-task generalization, SANODEP leverages trajectory-aware meta-learning to embed prior knowledge. In a penicillin production case study, SANODEP significantly outperforms GPs in the low-data regime, yielding improved objectives with fewer experimental runs and demonstrating robust generalization across on- and off-distribution batches, thereby accelerating optimization and reducing experimental costs.
2026.abstract: The optimisation of fed-batch (bio)chemical process recipes is subject to inherent, underlying, and unmeasurable fluctuations across batches, whose trajectories are difficult to model and costly to measure. Bayesian Optimisation (BayesOpt) is a powerful tool for sampling and optimisation of expensive-to-measure functions. Gaussian Processes (GPs), the surrogate models used in BayesOpt, are static, forecast poorly, and lack generalisation across experiments, limiting their applicability to time-varying batch processes with stochastic parameters, i.e., process fluctuations. This work investigates System-Aware Neural ODE Processes (SANODEP) as a meta-learning model to overcome the limitations of GPs and increase few-shot optimisation performance in BayesOpt. Using a penicillin batch production case study, we find that SANODEP outperforms GP-based BayesOpt in the low-data regime, resulting in improved objectives when few experimental runs are performed. These improvements are observed in both on- and off-distribution batches, highlighting the generalisation capabilities of SANODEP. Using this approach, batch process operators can accelerate the initial optimisation steps in BayesOpt by deploying meta-learning or optimise the process with fewer experiments when the experimental cost is high.

2026.title: BoGrape: Bayesian optimization over graphs with shortest-path encoded
2026.authors: Y Xie, S Zhang, J Qing, R Misener, C Tsay
2026.tldr: BoGrape introduces a principled Bayesian optimization framework for black-box objectives defined over *unseen graph structures* and node attributes, addressing limitations of fixed-graph BO. It leverages shortest-path graph kernels and a novel mixed-integer programming (MIP) formulation for acquisition optimization. This enables global exploration of combinatorial graph domains and explicit incorporation of problem-specific structural constraints. BoGrape demonstrates competitive performance on synthetic benchmarks and constrained molecular design case studies.
2026.abstract: Graph-structured data are central to many scientific and industrial applications where the goal is to optimize expensive black-box objectives defined over graph structures or node configurations -- as seen in molecular design, supply chains, and sensor placement. Bayesian optimization offers a principled approach for such settings, but existing methods largely focus on functions defined over nodes of a fixed graph. Moreover, graph optimization is often approached heuristically, and it remains unclear how to systematically incorporate structural constraints into BO. To address these gaps, we build on shortest-path graph kernels to develop a principled framework for acquisition optimization over unseen graph structures and associated node attributes. Through a novel formulation based on mixed-integer programming, we enable global exploration of the combinatorial domain over graph structures and explicit embedding of problem-specific constraints. We demonstrate that our method, BoGrape, is competitive both on general synthetic benchmarks and representative molecular design case studies with application-specific constraints.

2025.title: A Meta-Learning Approach for Few-Shot Bayesian Optimization of Batch Chemical Processes
2025.authors: B Langdon, G Patron, J Qing, C Kappatou, RM Lee, B Shafei, R Misener, ...
2025.tldr: Optimizing fed-batch chemical processes faces challenges from unmeasurable batch fluctuations, hindering standard Gaussian Processes (GPs) in Bayesian Optimization (BayesOpt). GPs lack generalization and struggle with time-varying, stochastic parameters. This work introduces **System-Aware Neural ODE Processes (SANODEP)** as a meta-learning model. SANODEP overcomes these GP limitations, significantly enhancing few-shot optimization performance in BayesOpt for complex, stochastic batch processes by improving forecasting and cross-experiment generalization.
2025.abstract: The optimisation of fed-batch (bio)chemical process recipes is subject to inherent, underlying, and unmeasurable fluctuations across batches, whose trajectories are difficult to model and costly to measure. Bayesian Optimisation (BayesOpt) is a powerful tool for sampling and optimisation of expensive-to-measure functions. Gaussian Processes (GPs), the surrogate models used in BayesOpt, are static, forecast poorly, and lack generalisation across experiments, limiting their applicability to time-varying batch processes with stochastic parameters, i.e., process fluctuations. This work investigates System-Aware Neural ODE Processes (SANODEP) as a meta-learning model to overcome the limitations of GPs and increase few-shot optimisation performance in BayesOpt.

2025.title: Global optimization of graph acquisition functions for neural architecture search
2025.authors: Y Xie, S Zhang, J Qing, R Misener, C Tsay
2025.tldr: This paper introduces NAS-GOAT, a novel method for globally optimizing graph acquisition functions in Neural Architecture Search (NAS). It addresses the challenge of discretely optimizing over weakly connected acyclic digraphs (DAGs) common in NAS. NAS-GOAT proposes an explicit Mixed-Integer Programming (MIP) formulation that precisely encodes graph search spaces, including properties like reachability and shortest paths. This encoding, compatible with shortest-path graph kernels and LCB acquisition functions, allows for global optimization with theoretical guarantees. Numerical results demonstrate NAS-GOAT's efficiency in finding optimal neural architectures on various benchmarks.
2025.abstract: Graph Bayesian optimization (BO) has shown potential as a powerful and data-efficient tool for neural architecture search (NAS). Most existing graph BO works focus on developing graph surrogates models, i.e., metrics of networks and/or different kernels to quantify the similarity between networks. However, the acquisition optimization, as a discrete optimization task over graph structures, is not well studied due to the complexity of formulating the graph search space and acquisition functions. This paper presents explicit optimization formulations for graph input space including properties such as reachability and shortest paths, which are used later to formulate graph kernels and the acquisition function. We theoretically prove that the proposed encoding is an equivalent representation of the graph space and provide restrictions for the NAS domain with either node or edge labels. Numerical results over several NAS benchmarks show that our method efficiently finds the optimal architecture for most cases, highlighting its efficacy.

2025.title: The catechol benchmark: Time-series solvent selection data for few-shot machine learning
2025.authors: T Boyne, JS Campos, BD Langdon, J Qing, Y Xie, S Zhang, C Tsay, ...
2025.tldr: This paper introduces "The catechol benchmark," a novel dataset comprising over 1200 transient flow process conditions for yield prediction, specifically targeting solvent selection. This first-ever continuous flow dataset, unlike previous discrete ones, presents new challenges for machine learning models. It serves as a benchmark for regression, transfer-learning, feature engineering, and active learning algorithms, offering direct applications in optimizing solvent replacement and promoting sustainable manufacturing.
2025.abstract: Machine learning has promised to change the landscape of laboratory chemistry, with impressive results in molecular property prediction and reaction retro-synthesis. However, chemical datasets are often inaccessible to the machine learning community as they tend to require cleaning, thorough understanding of the chemistry, or are simply not available. In this paper, we introduce a novel dataset for yield prediction, providing the first-ever transient flow dataset for machine learning benchmarking, covering over 1200 process conditions. While previous datasets focus on discrete parameters, our experimental set-up allow us to sample a large number of continuous process conditions, generating new challenges for machine learning models. We focus on solvent selection, a task that is particularly difficult to model theoretically and therefore ripe for machine learning applications. We showcase benchmarking for regression algorithms, transfer-learning approaches, feature engineering, and active learning, with important applications towards solvent replacement and sustainable manufacturing.

2025.title: System-Aware Neural ODE Processes for Few-Shot Bayesian Optimization
2025.authors: Jixiang Qing, Becky D Langdon, Robert M Lee, Behrang Shafei, Mark van der ...
2025.tldr: This paper introduces System-Aware Neural ODE Processes (SANODEP), extending Neural ODE Processes with a novel context embedding block to meta-learn unknown ODE systems from multiple trajectories. SANODEP forms the core of a few-shot Bayesian Optimization (BO) framework, which, coupled with a two-stage BO approach, efficiently optimizes initial conditions and termination times in dynamical systems despite costly, delayed evaluations. Experiments demonstrate SANODEP's effectiveness for few-shot BO and its adaptability to varying prior information levels.
2025.abstract: We consider the problem of optimizing initial conditions and termination time in dynamical systems governed by unknown ordinary differential equations (ODEs), where evaluating different initial conditions is costly and the state's value can not be measured in real-time but only with a delay while the measuring device processes the sample. To identify the optimal conditions in limited trials, we introduce a few-shot Bayesian Optimization (BO) framework based on the system's prior information. At the core of our approach is the System-Aware Neural ODE Processes (SANODEP), an extension of Neural ODE Processes (NODEP) designed to meta-learn ODE systems from multiple trajectories using a novel context embedding block. We further develop a two-stage BO framework to effectively incorporate search space constraints, enabling efficient optimization of both initial conditions and observation timings. We conduct extensive experiments showcasing SANODEP's potential for few-shot BO within dynamical systems. We also explore SANODEP's adaptability to varying levels of prior information, highlighting the trade-off between prior flexibility and model fitting accuracy.

2025.title: Molecular design using graph Bayesian optimization with shortest-path kernels
2025.authors: Y Xie, S Zhang, J Qing, R Misener, C Tsay
2025.venue: ICLR 2025 Workshop on Generative and Experimental Perspectives for …, 2025
2025.tldr: BoGrape presents a novel graph Bayesian optimization approach for molecular design, tackling expensive property evaluations and validity constraints. It leverages **shortest-path graph kernels** to efficiently measure molecular similarity and employs **mixed-integer programming** for global exploration while ensuring the feasibility of generated candidates. This method aims to generate optimal and valid molecular graphs given limited evaluations. Preliminary results demonstrate promising performance, bridging the gap between generative ML and practical molecular design.
2025.abstract: Past decades have seen the great potential of generative machine learning in molecular design while also exposed the gap between research contributions and practical applications. Considering the expensive-to-evaluate nature of molecular properties and hard-to-satisfy validity of molecular structures, this paper tackles molecular design from graph Bayesian optimization viewpoint, i.e., generating feasible and optimal molecular graph with compatible features given limited number of evaluations. Our proposed method, BoGrape, uses shortest-path graph kernels to measure the similarity between molecules and utilizes mixed-integer programming to allow global exploration of molecular space while maintaining the feasibility of generated candidates. Preliminary results show promising performance of BoGrape.

2024.title: Knee detection in Bayesian multi-objective optimization using Thompson sampling
2024.authors: A Heidari, J Qing, SR Gonzalez, J Branke, T Dhaene, I Couckuyt
2024.tldr: This paper proposes a novel Bayesian optimization framework using Thompson Sampling to efficiently detect knee regions in multi-objective problems. While estimating the entire Pareto front is computationally expensive, decision-makers often prioritize "knees" as attractive trade-offs. The method accurately locates single and multiple knee regions with a very small number of evaluations, offering a computationally and data-efficient approach for targeted optimization, circumventing the need for full Pareto front approximation.
2024.abstract: Real-world problems often consist of multiple conflicting objectives to be optimized simultaneously, featuring a set of Pareto-optimal solutions. Estimating the entire Pareto front can be computationally expensive, and is not always necessary, as decision makers will likely be interested only in specific regions of the Pareto front. In the absence of knowledge about the decision maker preferences, the so-called knees in the Pareto front are considered to be particularly attractive. In this paper, we propose using Thompson Sampling in the Bayesian optimization framework to estimate the location of the knee regions in a data-efficient manner. Our experimental results show that the proposed methods accurately locate the knee regions after a very small number of evaluations, providing a computationally efficient approach to single-and multi-knee detection in multi-objective optimization.

2024.title: Wind turbine hybrid physics-based deep learning model for a health monitoring approach considering provision of ancillary services
2024.authors: N Kayedpour, J Qing, J Wauters, JDM De Kooning, I Couckuyt, ...
2024.venue: IEEE Transactions on Instrumentation and Measurement 73, 1-14, 2024
2024.tldr: This paper proposes a novel hybrid physics-based deep learning framework for NREL's 5-MW wind turbine health monitoring. It accurately models time-varying control-response correlations and aerodynamic nonlinearity. A computationally efficient weakly supervised method, leveraging this hybrid structure, detects degradations and anomalies under curtailment operations. This is complemented by a self-learning classifier that adapts to unforeseen abnormalities. The approach effectively handles system uncertainties like wind stochasticity and data sparsity, significantly improving the accuracy and efficiency of wind turbine condition assessment.
2024.abstract: Assessing the overall condition of wind turbines (WTs) in operation is challenging due to their intricate nature. This becomes even more complicated when WTs provide ancillary services and respond to grid requirements under curtailment modes. Multiple models are required to effectively evaluate the WTs’ healthy condition, which can be unmanageable and impractical, particularly for large-scale wind farms. This article proposes a novel hybrid physics-based deep learning framework to accurately approximate the time-varying correlation between control sequences and system response, reflecting the aerodynamic nonlinearity of the 5-MW offshore WT model, designed and tested by the National Renewable Energy Laboratory (NREL). Another layer of this study’s novelty relies on proposing a computationally efficient weakly supervised method that uses the hybrid structure to detect degradations and anomalies considering curtailment operation. Then, a self-learning classification approach is employed to iteratively update the best-tuned classifier, dynamically learning unforeseen abnormalities from brand-new anomalies during active operations. The proposed anomaly detection strategy deals with system uncertainties, such as wind stochasticity, power curve variations, and different sparsity levels in the datasets. The results of the proposed approach show promise in improving health monitoring performance, leading to a more efficient and accurate assessment of the overall condition of WTs.

2024.title: 5.4 Surrogate Models for Bayesian Optimization
2024.authors: S Adriaensen, N Bartoli, M Binois, R Gramacy, R Le Riche, SH Ng, ...

2023.title: A robust multi-objective Bayesian optimization framework considering input uncertainty
2023.authors: J Qing, I Couckuyt, T Dhaene
2023.tldr: This paper introduces a novel Bayesian optimization framework for multi-objective problems considering input uncertainty. It proposes a robust Gaussian Process model to infer the Bayes risk criterion, quantifying solution robustness. A two-stage Bayesian optimization process then searches for a robust Pareto frontier, identifying solutions with good average performance under uncertainty. The framework supports various input uncertainty distributions, leverages parallel computing, and demonstrates effectiveness through numerical benchmarks.
2023.abstract: Bayesian optimization is a popular tool for optimizing time-consuming objective functions with a limited number of function evaluations. In real-life applications like engineering design, the designer often wants to take multiple objectives as well as input uncertainty into account to find a set of robust solutions. While this is an active topic in single-objective Bayesian optimization, it is less investigated in the multi-objective case. We introduce a novel Bayesian optimization framework to perform multi-objective optimization considering input uncertainty. We propose a robust Gaussian Process model to infer the Bayes risk criterion to quantify robustness, and we develop a two-stage Bayesian optimization process to search for a robust Pareto frontier, i.e., solutions that have good average performance under input uncertainty. The complete framework supports various distributions of the input uncertainty and takes full advantage of parallel computing. We demonstrate the effectiveness of the framework through numerical benchmarks.

2023.title: Trieste: Efficiently exploring the depths of black-box functions with tensorflow
2023.authors: V Picheny, J Berkeley, HB Moss, H Stojic, U Granta, SW Ober, A Artemev, ...
2023.tldr: Trieste is an open-source Python package for scalable Bayesian Optimization (BO) and active learning, leveraging TensorFlow 2. It offers a highly modular framework for efficient black-box function exploration, integrating TensorFlow-based models (GPflow, Keras) and customizable acquisition functions. The package optimizes for TF2's auto-differentiation and GPU support, meticulously avoiding expensive graph retracing during sequential BO loops. Its `AskTellOptimizer` interface enables flexible, real-world interactive BO, positioning Trieste as a robust, research-friendly, and production-ready toolkit.
2023.abstract: We present Trieste, an open-source Python package for Bayesian optimization and active learning benefiting from the scalability and efficiency of TensorFlow. Our library enables the plug-and-play of popular TensorFlow-based models within sequential decision-making loops, e.g. Gaussian processes from GPflow or GPflux, or neural networks from Keras. This modular mindset is central to the package and extends to our acquisition functions and the internal dynamics of the decision-making loop, both of which can be tailored and extended by researchers or engineers when tackling custom use cases. Trieste is a research-friendly and production-ready toolkit backed by a comprehensive test suite, extensive documentation, and available at https://github.com/secondmind-labs/trieste.

2023.title: Bayesian active learning for engineering design and optimization under uncertainty
2023.tldr: This research applies Bayesian Active Learning (BAL) to address computationally expensive engineering design and optimization under uncertainty. The core contribution involves devising novel sequential optimal designs built upon Bayesian models. These BAL strategies enable automatic, efficient tuning of product parameters, leading to superior design configurations with significantly fewer costly simulations compared to traditional iterative methods.
2023.abstract: Practical engineering design is a complex problem that involves iteratively tuning product parameters to find satisfactory performance. Evaluating performance typically involves time-consuming or costly simulations, demanding algorithms that require fewer evaluations. The rapid evolution of machine learning has quickly provided opportunities for such problems, where model-based adaptive tuning algorithms can be devised. This dissertation contributes to this effort by exploring Bayesian models and Active Learning techniques built upon them, to devise new sequential optimal designs for various problems and objectives. The ultimate goal is to achieve automatic tuning to obtain better design configurations that are more computationally efficient.

2023.title: {PF} ²ES: Parallel Feasible Pareto Frontier Entropy Search for Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization
2023.authors: J Qing, HB Moss, T Dhaene, I Couckuyt
2023.venue: 17th Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS), 2023

2022.title: Finding knees in bayesian multi-objective optimization
2022.authors: A Heidari, J Qing, S Rojas Gonzalez, J Branke, T Dhaene, I Couckuyt
2022.venue: International Conference on Parallel Problem Solving from Nature, 104-117, 2022
2022.tldr: This paper proposes novel acquisition functions within a Bayesian Optimization framework to efficiently find knee points in multi-objective optimization. Acknowledging that decision-makers often prefer specific trade-offs over the full Pareto front, the approach detects knees (based on two definitions) with limited evaluations. This method scales to many objectives, demonstrating promising results on various benchmarks for identifying desirable solutions data-efficiently.
2022.abstract: Multi-objective optimization requires many evaluations to identify a sufficiently dense approximation of the Pareto front. Especially for a higher number of objectives, extracting the Pareto front might not be easy nor cheap. On the other hand, the Decision-Maker is not always interested in the entire Pareto front, and might prefer a solution where there is a desirable trade-off between different objectives. An example of an attractive solution is the knee point of the Pareto front, although the current literature differs on the definition of a knee. In this work, we propose to detect knee solutions in a data-efficient manner (i.e., with a limited number of time-consuming evaluations), according to two definitions of knees. In particular, we propose several novel acquisition functions in the Bayesian Optimization framework for detecting these knees, which allows for scaling to many objectives. The suggested acquisition functions are evaluated on various benchmarks with promising results.

2022.title: Adaptive sampling with automatic stopping for feasible region identification in engineering design
2022.authors: J Qing, N Knudde, F Garbuglia, D Spina, I Couckuyt, T Dhaene
2022.tldr: This paper introduces an adaptive sampling methodology using Gaussian process metamodels for efficient feasible region identification in engineering design problems with multiple constraints. It employs an information-based sequential sampling strategy for refining prediction accuracy. A novel contribution is a framework for automatically stopping the adaptive sampling process by accurately estimating the metamodel's prediction accuracy, demonstrating improved efficiency and robustness compared to state-of-the-art methods.
2022.abstract: Engineering design is a complex process to find a suitable trade-off among different, and sometimes conflicting, design specifications. In reality, these requirements can be often considered as constraints of the design problem, that can be defined in terms of performance measures or geometrical characteristics of the device under study. In this paper, a new design space exploration methodology is presented for discovering feasible regions in the design space, where the term feasible region indicates the set of all design configurations satisfying all constraints of the design problem. The proposed method is based on Gaussian process metamodels to estimate the feasible region and leverages a information-based adaptive sampling technique to sequentially refine the prediction accuracy, which is applicable for multiple constraints problems. To efficiently stop the adaptive sampling process, a novel framework to estimate the metamodel’s prediction accuracy is proposed. The efficiency, accuracy and robustness of the proposed approach are compared with state-of-art techniques on suitable benchmark problems and practical engineering examples.

2022.title: A robust Bayesian optimization framework for microwave circuit design under uncertainty
2022.authors: D De Witte, J Qing, I Couckuyt, T Dhaene, D Vande Ginste, D Spina
2022.tldr: This paper presents a robust Bayesian Optimization (BO) framework for microwave circuit design addressing parameter uncertainty. It achieves robustness by modifying the expected improvement (EI) criterion to account for design variations. The data-efficient BO minimizes simulations while identifying robust designs. Validation demonstrates significantly improved design robustness compared to standard methods.
2022.abstract: In modern electronics, there are many inevitable uncertainties and variations of design parameters that have a profound effect on the performance of a device. These are, among others, induced by manufacturing tolerances, assembling inaccuracies, material diversities, machining errors, etc. This prompts wide interests in enhanced optimization algorithms that take the effect of these uncertainty sources into account and that are able to find robust designs, i.e., designs that are insensitive to the uncertainties early in the design cycle. In this work, a novel machine learning-based optimization framework that accounts for uncertainty of the design parameters is presented. This is achieved by using a modified version of the expected improvement criterion. Moreover, a data-efficient Bayesian Optimization framework is leveraged to limit the number of simulations required to find a robust design solution. Two suitable application examples validate that the robustness is significantly improved compared to standard design methods.

2022.title: Spectral representation of robustness measures for optimization under input uncertainty
2022.authors: J Qing, T Dhaene, I Couckuyt
2022.tldr: This paper proposes a Spectral Representation of Robustness Measures for efficient inference of mean-variance robustness under Gaussian Processes (GPs), circumventing challenging Bayesian variance inference. Leveraging GP spectral representation with Fourier features, this analytical approach approximates robustness for normal and uniform input uncertainties. Integrated into robust Bayesian Optimization acquisition functions, the method demonstrates competitive performance on benchmarks and real-world applications, effectively quantifying and optimizing for robustness.
2022.abstract: We study the inference of mean-variance robustness measures to quantify input uncertainty under the Gaussian Process (GP) framework. These measures are widely used in applications where the robustness of the solution is of interest, for example, in engineering design. While the variance is commonly used to characterize the robustness, Bayesian inference of the variance using GPs is known to be challenging. In this paper, we propose a Spectral Representation of Robustness Measures based on the GP’s spectral representation, i.e., an analytical approach to approximately infer both robustness measures for normal and uniform input uncertainty distributions. We present two approximations based on different Fourier features and compare their accuracy numerically. To demonstrate their utility and efficacy in robust Bayesian Optimization, we integrate the analytical robustness measures in three standard acquisition functions for various robust optimization formulations. We show their competitive performance on numerical benchmarks and real-life applications.

2021.title: Hovering efficiency optimization of the ducted propeller with weight penalty taken into account
2021.authors: Y Hu, J xiang Qing, ZH Liu, ZJ Conrad, JN Cao, XP Zhang
2021.tldr: This paper optimizes ducted propeller design for hovering efficiency, incorporating structural weight. It finds that weight penalty is crucial at low disk loading, favoring lighter structures, while aerodynamic efficiency dominates at high disk loading. Multi-objective optimization identifies designs where ducted propellers still surpass open propellers in system efficiency at low disk loadings. Optimal configurations feature a large inner lip (most impactful for efficiency), small outer lip, and short/no diffuser, achieving significant weight reduction with limited aerodynamic loss, leading to low height-to-diameter ratios for easier integration.
2021.abstract: The ducted propeller is superior to the open propeller in hovering efficiency. However, the overall system efficiency of a ducted propeller is reduced due to its heavy structure. If the weight penalty is taken into account, will the ducted propeller still be superior to an open propeller? And in this scenario, how will a ducted propeller with better efficiency than an open propeller be designed? This paper investigates these questions by parametric analysis based on experiments and then parametric optimization that involves hovering efficiency and structural weight in objective functions. Both multi-disciplinary design optimization and multi-objective programming are performed by surrogate-based optimization. An in-house automatic structured mesh generation module is developed to deal with significant geometry variation in design space. Finally, the optimization results are validated by post-optimization experiments. The results of experiment and optimization indicate that the effects of weight penalty play a leading role at low disk loading and hence in this case, the one with lighter structure is superior. But at high disk loading, as thrust gets higher, the leading factor turns into aerodynamic hovering efficiency, therefore the one with higher aerodynamic hovering efficiency prevails. The multi-objective optimization produces an L-shaped Pareto front, and the optimum of multi-disciplinary optimization is quite close to the Pareto front knee point. The designs in this region encounter limited aerodynamic hovering efficiency loss but gain significant weight reduction. Therefore, we can obtain a ducted propeller superior to an open propeller in system efficiency with pretty low disk loading, although the weight penalty is considered. These designs feature a relatively large inner lip radius, a small outer lip radius, and a short or even no diffuser. This means that the inner lip radius contributes the most to the aerodynamic hovering efficiency, followed by the diffuser and outer lip. These designs have very low height to diameter ratio therefore they can be easily integrated into aircraft structure.

2021.title: Bayesian active learning for multi‐objective feasible region identification in microwave devices
2021.authors: F Garbuglia, J Qing, N Knudde, D Spina, I Couckuyt, D Deschrijver, ...
2021.tldr: This paper introduces a novel Bayesian active learning framework for efficient multi-objective feasible region identification in microwave device design. It leverages a stochastic model to accurately map designs satisfying specifications while significantly reducing the number of simulations required. The framework provides an automated and efficient procedure, validated through an application example demonstrating its effectiveness in rapidly discovering suitable device designs.
2021.abstract: In microwave device and circuit design, many simulations are often needed to find a set of designs that satisfy one or multiple specifications chosen by the designer upfront: the feasible region. A novel Bayesian active learning framework is presented to accurately identify the feasible region with a low number of simulations. The technique leverages on a stochastic model to obtain an efficient and automated procedure. A suitable application example validates the proposed technique and shows its effectiveness to rapidly obtain many suitable designs.

2020.title: Batch Bayesian active learning for feasible region identification by local penalization
2020.authors: J Qing, N Knudde, I Couckuyt, T Dhaene, K Shintani
2020.tldr: This paper introduces a batch Bayesian active learning technique for efficient feasible region identification, addressing the limitation of sequential sampling in expensive constraint evaluations. Leveraging available computational resources, the method selects multiple samples per iteration, assuming Lipschitz continuity of the constraint function. It also extends current state-of-the-art batch methods for this task. Experiments demonstrate the proposed technique's superior performance over these extended batch strategies.
2020.abstract: Identifying all designs satisfying a set of constraints is an important part of the engineering design process. With physics-based simulation codes, evaluating the constraints becomes considerable expensive. Active learning can provide an elegant approach to efficiently characterize the feasible region, i.e., the set of feasible designs. Although active learning strategies have been proposed for this task, most of them are dealing with adding just one sample per iteration as opposed to selecting multiple samples per iteration, also known as batch active learning. While this is efficient with respect to the amount of information gained per iteration, it neglects available computation resources. We propose a batch Bayesian active learning technique for feasible region identification by assuming that the constraint function is Lipschitz continuous. In addition, we extend current state-of-the-art batch methods to also handle feasible region identification. Experiments show better performance of the proposed method than the extended batch methods.

2020.title: Bayesian active learning for electromagnetic structure design
2020.authors: J Qing, N Knudde, I Couckuyt, D Spina, T Dhaene
2020.venue: 2020 14th European Conference on Antennas and Propagation (EuCAP), 1-5, 2020
2020.tldr: This paper presents a Bayesian active learning framework for designing electromagnetic structures. It leverages an entropy search-based strategy with a Gaussian Process model to efficiently identify design configurations that satisfy specific requirements. The core contribution is minimizing the number of time-consuming computer simulations or expensive experimental trials needed to achieve desired design specifications, thereby accelerating the design process.
2020.abstract: A novel design framework based on Bayesian active learning is presented in this contribution. The proposed approach allows one to identify a set of design configurations satisfying the chosen specification. In particular, the entropy search-based active learning strategy, which relies on a Gaussian Process model, is able to minimize the number of time-consuming computer simulations or expensive design trials necessary to reach this goal. A suitable application example validates the proposed method.

2019.title: Kriging Assisted Integrated Rotor-Duct Optimization for Ducted Fan in Hover
2019.authors: J Qing, Y Hu, Y Wang, Z Liu, X Fu, W Liu
2019.tldr: This paper presents a Kriging-assisted integrated rotor-duct optimization for ducted fans in hover, simultaneously optimizing both components using RANS. This approach addresses crucial rotor-duct interactions, unlike prior separate optimizations. Key findings reveal that integrated design improves hovering efficiency by obtaining blades with longer tip chords. This injects more momentum into the duct's boundary layer, suppressing flow separation and allowing for larger diffuser expansion angles, ultimately leading to superior overall performance.
2019.abstract: The design of ducted fan was primarily based on parametric analysis and the existing optimization design studies mainly focus on either the rotor or the duct alone. However, the interactions between the rotor and duct remarkably affects the performance of the ducted fan. Therefore, it has been expected that an integrated optimization such the rotor-duct interactions are involved could result in a better design. In this paper, the integrated rotor-duct optimization was performed. Then it was compared with several different optimized configurations. The Reynolds-Averaged Navier-Stokes solver incorporated with momentum source method was adopted to predict performance of ducted fan and it was validated by force measurement experiments. The duct shape was parameterized by the FFD method and the blade shape was modeled by Bezier splines. A surrogate based optimization framework using Kriging model was developed. The hovering efficiency was set as the objective function subjecting to the thrust constraint. The optima from different optimized configurations were analyzed with the help of crossover studies. The analysis revealed that the improvement of the ducted fan hovering efficiency is primarily restricted by the flow separations in the duct. When the shape of both the rotor and duct was involved into the design optimization, the blade with longer chord at blade tip was obtained. This helps injecting more momentum into the boundary layer of the duct and the flow separation can be suppressed. Therefore, the integrated rotor-duct optimization produces the duct with larger diffuser expansion angle and better hovering efficiency.
